name: What happens if the yard drainage is poor before building a spa?

mainEntity.name: What happens if the yard drainage is poor before building a spa?
mainEntity.text: What happens if the yard drainage is poor before building a spa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Poor drainage is one of the biggest risks in custom spa construction because water always finds the lowest point. If the yard already collects water, the spa area may need grading changes, drains, or additional site work before construction begins. Ignoring drainage can lead to settlement, puddling, erosion around the spa, and damage to finishes or adjacent hardscape. It can also make the spa area less comfortable and harder to maintain. In some Los Angeles properties, drainage is complicated by slope, neighboring runoff, or limited yard space, so solving the issue may require a more detailed site plan. Homeowners should ask the contractor how runoff will move around the spa in both everyday use and heavy rain. A spa should be built on a site that manages water well, not one that depends on luck.
acceptedAnswer.description: Poor drainage can damage a custom spa project by causing settlement, standing water, finish problems, and long-term maintenance issues. Drainage problems should be fixed before construction or built into the site plan.
